features.description: Prospective marker meaning fixing to/about to.
features.blocked_context: Use only when the anchor expresses near-future action.

features.description: Reflexive pronoun form.
features.safe_example: He blamed hisself for the mistake.
features.blocked_context: Use only where a reflexive pronoun already exists.

features.description: Lexical item referring to family or relatives.
features.blocked_context: Do not add family relationships absent from the anchor.

features.description: Reduced form of trying to.
features.safe_example: The student is tryna explain the reason.
features.blocked_context: Use only where trying to already exists or is directly implied.

features.description: Dialectal lexical/phonological form corresponding to asked.
features.blocked_context: High risk as orthographic/phonological marking; avoid unless specifically approved.

features.description: Invariant be marks habitual or repeated action/state.
features.blocked_context: Do not replace every is/are with be; use only for habitual meaning.

features.description: Preverbal done marks completed action or resultant state.
features.blocked_context: Use only when the anchor already expresses completion.

features.description: Remote past marker for a state or event that began long ago.
features.blocked_context: Use only when remote past meaning is already present; do not turn recent past into long-term past.

features.description: Habitual frequentative marker for repeated or persistent events.
features.safe_example: He stay asking questions in class.
features.blocked_context: Use only where repeated/frequent action is already stated.

features.description: Omission of forms of be in specific grammatical contexts.
features.blocked_context: Do not omit be in contexts not licensed by the grammar; requires careful review.

features.description: Multiple negative elements expressing one semantic negation.
features.blocked_context: Use only where a negative meaning already exists; do not add or strengthen negation.

features.description: Negative element appears before auxiliary/subject order in some clauses.
features.blocked_context: Too likely to change emphasis or readability; keep for review-only inventory.

features.description: Present-tense third-person verbs may appear without Standard English -s.
features.safe_example: She walk to school every day.
features.blocked_context: Use only in present-tense third-person contexts where the subject and time reference stay unchanged.

features.description: Use of them as a demonstrative before plural nouns.
features.blocked_context: Use only when a plural demonstrative already exists or is naturally available.

features.description: Relative clauses without an overt relative pronoun in subject position.
features.safe_example: The person helped him was kind.
features.blocked_context: Review-only because omission can reduce clarity in educational answers.

features.description: Short linked clauses maintaining the same topic.
features.safe_example: He kept trying. Kept going even after failing.
features.blocked_context: Do not remove rubric-relevant reasoning while shortening.
features.source_reference: DART Appendix A; Labov, Ash, and Boberg, 2006

features.description: Orthographic representations listed in Appendix A.
features.blocked_context: Avoid mocking or racialized eye-dialect spellings unless explicitly approved for orthographic perturbation.

features.description: Negative auxiliary form used across AAE and other English varieties.
features.blocked_context: Use only where a negative auxiliary already exists; do not add negation.
features.source_reference: Green, 2002; Rickford, 1999; Yale Grammatical Diversity Project

features.description: Omission of be only where Standard English contraction would be possible.
features.blocked_context: Use only in contractible present-tense be contexts; do not remove be where it changes tense, emphasis, or clarity.
features.source_reference: DART Appendix A; Labov, 1972; Green, 2002; Rickford, 1999

features.description: Possessive noun phrase without Standard English possessive -s.
features.blocked_context: Use only where possession already exists; avoid proper names if it reduces clarity.

features.description: Marker of sustained or intensified activity.
features.safe_example: The character steady tries even after failing.
features.blocked_context: Use only where ongoing/persistent activity is already present.

disallowed_features: features not licensed by the inventory
safety_notes: Do not make the response sound less intelligent, less academic, or stereotyped.
Prefer tense/aspect features only when the anchor already contains the needed time meaning.
